A thesis prepared at the Manned Spacecraft Center in Houston presents this speech study. It advances a method for cutting recorded speech into its natural parts. The method studies the spacing between zero crossings of the sound wave. Earlier work needed slow computer analysis of those patterns. The thesis set out to remove that bottleneck.

The author designed and built an electronic analyzer that works in real time. The paper reviews why speech segmentation matters and then tests the design ideas. It concludes that the design concept works and that the device can really be built. Computer analysis was no longer required to use the best part of the method.
